proposal.description: The strike clear fires when the clean count is at or above clean_run_target, while the clean-run counter itself saturates only on an exact match
proposal.reason: Say the host lowers clean_run_target in mid-run to below the clean count already reached. The original counter runs on past the new target and wraps before it matches, so strike_level stays nonzero for about 2**CLEAN_RUN_W more switching cycles. With this mutant strike_level drops to 0 on the next clock.

proposal.description: A window_trip on the clock the clean run completes cancels the strike forgiveness, although the run had already earned it
proposal.reason: Say window_trip is asserted on the first clock where clean_counter equals clean_run_target. The original zeroes strike_level on that edge. The mutant keeps the old count, so the hiccup that follows adds to it, and it can set latch_assert (for example with 2 strikes and max_strikes=3) where the original would only go to 1 strike.

proposal.description: The clean-run streak is broken by leaving S_RUN for any state except S_HICCUP, so a completed clean count survives into the cool-down
proposal.reason: Say hiccup_active rises as run_active falls after a completed clean run, with no window_trip on that clock. The clean count stays at clean_run_target through the cool-down, so one clock after the entry the clean branch zeroes the strike that hiccup just added. strike_level drops back to 0 during S_HICCUP, and repeated hiccups never set latch_assert.

proposal.description: The clean-run clear is nested inside hiccup_entry instead of being its sibling, so a completed clean run is forgiven only when the next hiccup begins (the count restarts at one strike)
proposal.reason: After a completed clean run, strike_level keeps its old nonzero value for the rest of S_RUN instead of dropping to 0. On the next hiccup entry the latch test still reads that old count, so with 2 earlier strikes and max_strikes=3 latch_assert trips on the first hiccup after a long fault-free run.
